title: Tiered Metal evidence — declared parity obligation, not directory ancestry
status: PREREGISTERED BUT NOT FROZEN — the classification prediction is frozen; numeric baselines are deferred, see baseline.deferred_because
claim: A pull request pays full behavioural Metal qualification only when it changes the Metal crate or a DECLARED parity obligation. An upstream change that can break the compile but not the numbers pays a compile plus the ordinary-profile witness. Everything else pays no macOS time.

measurement_contract.inherits: docs/ci-throughput/E2-contract.json — every prediction names an INTENSIVE metric, and the instrument refuses extensive metrics across samples of different size
measurement_contract.instrument_change_required_before_freezi: workflow_exec_max is keyed on WORKFLOW. Under E2-D one workflow emits both a ~24-minute tier-A job and a ~2-minute tier-B job, so its p50 becomes a mixture that hides the per-tier story. E2-D needs job_exec_max.<workflow>.<job> before D1 or D3 can be scored at all.

baseline.deferred_because: The post-E2-A steady state does not exist yet: A1 stands at n=2 (24.87 and 23.00 min against a 56.61-minute pre-E2-A baseline) and its contract asks for n>=8. Freezing a numeric baseline now would bake in a two-sample estimate as the thing D is scored against.
baseline.collection_rule: Freeze when workflow_exec_max.larql-compute-metal.n >= 8 under E2-A, using the same --since windowing discipline as E1: a date strictly after the E2-A merge (2026-09-07), never a window that straddles it.

frozen_now.what: The classification prediction, which is derivable from data that already exists and must not be re-derived after D runs.
frozen_now.sample: pull requests #415-#449, 35 with file data, 18 triggering the Metal gate today (6 metal-touching, 12 upstream-only)
frozen_now.falsifier: If the live triage job assigns a different tier to any of these 18 pull requests than the replay did, the classifier and the replay disagree and neither can be cited until that is resolved.

predictions.claim: at least half of Metal-triggering attempts receive tier B
predictions.reason: the replay puts 11 of 18 at tier B; the band allows for a live mix that differs from a 35-pull-request sample
predictions.falsifier: below 0.3 means the declared obligations are so broad that tiering buys nothing, and the manifest needs narrowing before the mechanism is worth its complexity

predictions.claim: macOS executed runner-minutes per attempt fall by at least 35% from the post-E2-A baseline
predictions.reason: 11 of 18 triggers move from ~24 min to ~2 min, and msrv-metal folds into the tier-B job
predictions.falsifier: a fall of less than 15% means the tiering did not reach the macOS pool

predictions.claim: VALIDITY — the tier-A gate itself is unchanged, within 10%
predictions.reason: D must not appear to work by making the full gate cheaper. If tier-A duration moves, D has changed what full qualification MEANS and D1/D2 are not measuring what they claim.
predictions.falsifier: a tier-A p50 more than 10% from the E2-A baseline IN EITHER DIRECTION means the full gate was altered and the effect predictions must not be read. Two-sided deliberately: a tier-A gate that got FASTER has had work removed from it, and one that got SLOWER is no longer the gate A1 measured. Either way D1/D2 are not measuring what they claim.
predictions.condition_note: Uses abs_delta_pct, not delta_pct. Conditions are ANDed, so a single delta_pct clause cannot express 'more than 10% away in either direction' — written as {lt: -10} it silently drops the upper half and a +20% slowdown returns PARTIAL rather than FALSIFIED. That is how this entry was first written; ci_throughput.py's selftest now carries the control that catches it.

predictions.claim: macOS queue wait p50 falls by at least 20%
predictions.reason: E1's BASELINE analysis identified scheduling units as the hypothesised mechanism: the jobs c2 targeted carried disproportionate queue cost relative to execution — quality's msrv-macOS leg was 33 jobs, 544 queue-minutes and 22 execution-minutes. E2-D tests that mechanism on an intensive metric. It is NOT inherited from a C2 result: C2 returned INVALID COMPARISON and remains unadjudicated, so the mechanism is a live hypothesis here, not an established finding.
predictions.falsifier: no movement means the removed jobs were not the ones contending — the same falsifier c2 carried, now on a metric that can actually be scored
predictions.provenance_note: Wording corrected 2026-09-07. An earlier draft said E1's C2 'established that the macOS win comes from removing scheduling units, not compute'. C2 established no such thing: it was INVALID COMPARISON. What E1 produced was a pre-intervention measurement of the asymmetry plus post-hoc diagnostics in E1-postmortem.md. Citing an unadjudicated mechanism as established is the failure this programme exists to avoid.

structural_falsifiers.claim: no pull request touching a declared parity path ever receives tier B
structural_falsifiers.check: replay every pull request in the live AFTER window through metal_tier.py and assert no attempt whose diff intersects parity_obligations was assigned B. This is the SAFETY property; D1-D4 are throughput and none of them would notice a wrong answer here.

structural_falsifiers.claim: the manifest is complete with respect to what the Metal crate references
structural_falsifiers.check: scripts/metal_tier.py check exits 0. Must run in CI, not by hand, or it is the vacuous gate this programme keeps finding.

structural_falsifiers.claim: the tier-B job actually fails on an upstream API break
structural_falsifiers.check: deliberately change a signature in a declared interface_only path so the Metal crate cannot compile; the compat job must red. A green tier B on a real break is the failure mode that makes tiering unsafe. Dispatch on a throwaway branch, as S2/S3 were.

structural_falsifiers.claim: the triage job and the offline replay agree
structural_falsifiers.check: the tier the live triage assigns equals the tier metal_tier.py assigns to the same diff, for every attempt in the AFTER window.

confounds: The replay classifies against TODAY's tree; a file that moved since a pull request landed classifies by where it lives now.

Five manifest entries carry confidence=needs_review and are tier A by the safety asymmetry rather than by a positive finding. Resolving them can only move pull requests from A to B, so D1 and D2 are conservative as frozen.
E2-E (reusing a qualification across pushes within one pull request) would also reduce macOS minutes. It must not land inside D's measurement window.

mechanisms.tiering: run the evidence proportional to the claim a change can invalidate
mechanisms.contention: remove macOS scheduling units, not macOS compute
